_disclaimer: RESEARCH FINDINGS, NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Values are transcribed verbatim from the dataset's own metadata.license field; they are not a legal opinion, and (see conflicts below) they are not necessarily correct.
claim_under_test: DATASET-DESIGN-reservoir.md §7 item 2: 'common-pile/libretexts_filtered carries metadata.license; filter on it rather than assuming the collection is uniform.'
verdict: VERIFIED, BOTH HALVES. (a) The field exists as a real typed struct member. (b) The collection is genuinely NON-uniform - 7 distinct values - so filtering rather than assuming is the correct instruction.

schema_evidence.metadata_is: a struct, NOT a free-form JSON string - so it is queryable server-side
schema_evidence.verified: YES - metadata.license is present in the declared feature schema and populated in every row.

method.approach: NO DOWNLOAD. Exact server-side aggregation via the datasets-server /filter endpoint (DuckDB-backed), which returns num_rows_total for a WHERE clause. Every count below is an EXACT full-corpus count, not a sample extrapolation.
method.distinct_value_discovery: Iterative exclusion: repeatedly query `license IS NOT NULL AND license <> <each value already found>`, take one row, then count that value exactly. Terminated when the residual query returned num_rows_total=0, which PROVES the enumeration is complete.
method.completeness_proof: The 7 exact counts sum to 40049 = num_examples exactly, and the residual set was empty. No value was missed.
method.sampling_caveat: The /first-rows sample (32 rows) showed only ONE license value and would have been badly misleading. Reported distribution is from full-corpus counts instead.

key_findings: ZERO non-commercial rows. No NC variant appears anywhere in libretexts_filtered (verified: LIKE '%by-nc%' -> 0, LIKE '%NonCommercial%' -> 0). Common Pile filtered NC content OUT before publishing. So for THIS corpus the NC question is already answered - but see the conflict finding, which is why you should still record it.

1948 rows (4.86%) are NOT Creative Commons at all: 1191 'Public Domain' + 757 'GNU Free Documentation License'. The design doc's 'declares licenses per page' framing is right, but a reader who assumes 'CC variant' as the value domain will mis-parse ~5% of rows. The _licenses.parquet schema must NOT model the value as a CC-only enum.

Share-alike is 32.0% (12836 rows: by-sa 4.0/3.0/2.5). That collides with DATASET-DESIGN §7 item 4 (share-alike segregation), which currently names only FineWiki and StackExchange. LibreTexts is a THIRD share-alike source and should be added there.
Version drift within the same variant: by-sa appears at 4.0, 3.0 AND 2.5; by appears at 4.0 and 3.0. Store the version separately from the variant or version-specific obligations become unqueryable.

conflict_with_openstax_upstream.severity: HIGH - this is the finding that justifies recording licenses per book even though libretexts_filtered has zero NC rows
conflict_with_openstax_upstream.what_was_measured: 7121 rows (17.8% of the corpus) have metadata.author LIKE '%OpenStax%'. Their declared licenses: 6974 CC BY 4.0, 126 CC BY-SA 4.0, 19 Public Domain, 2 CC BY 3.0. ZERO NC.
conflict_with_openstax_upstream.why_that_is_suspicious: OpenStax's own APIs declare 73 of its 84 live books (86.9%) as CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. LibreTexts relabels OpenStax-derived pages as CC BY 4.0 - dropping the NC clause - at scale.
conflict_with_openstax_upstream.affected_rows_caveat: 1375 is a NON-EXHAUSTIVE lower bound from 5 URL probes only. The true figure is bounded above by the 6974 OpenStax-attributed CC BY 4.0 rows. Some OpenStax books ARE genuinely CC BY (e.g. 1st-edition College Physics is CC BY 4.0 while College Physics 2e is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), so the two sources are not automatically in conflict on every title - resolution requires per-title edition matching, which was NOT done here.
conflict_with_openstax_upstream.implication: metadata.license cannot be treated as authoritative on its own. A commercial-use query answered purely from LibreTexts metadata would return CLEAN for content whose upstream publisher asserts NC. This is exactly why the schema below carries license_source/license_authority per row rather than one license column.
conflict_with_openstax_upstream.not_a_legal_claim: Which party is correct is a legal question and is NOT resolved here. The finding is that the two declarations DISAGREE and the disagreement is machine-detectable.
